architecture_principles: a discovered material regularity is only usable inside the chemistry family in which it was measured
a scientific applicability boundary is executable code, not prompt advice
the language model may criticize the rule and may not override it
value of information is computed by a deterministic tool over the admissible set only
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
every gate decision carries a machine-readable reason and is serialized with the run

arm_difference_declaration.forbidden_confound: Hiding applicability information from V5_NO_GATE while showing it to V5_FULL is prohibited by protocol v1.1.
held_identical: model endpoint and stage model assignment
evidence access profile and filtered evidence state
raw assess_shared_shape_applicability outputs for every candidate
the full inadmissible-card list and its machine-readable reasons
VOI implementation, weights and tie epsilon
arm_difference_declaration.information_parity_evidence: build_pre_enforcement_payload() takes no arm argument, and its SHA-256 is written into every run as pre_enforcement_payload_sha256. The two arms must report the same hash.
arm_difference_declaration.only_intended_difference: whether the identical chemistry-domain applicability audit is enforced as hard experiment-card admissibility before VOI and at freeze
arm_difference_declaration.payload_consequence: Both arms receive the same audit, the same per-candidate applicability outputs and the same inadmissible-card list. V5_NO_GATE marks the audit advisory and keeps every card selectable; V5_FULL marks it binding and removes the inadmissible cards from the ranked set.

candidate_space.rationale: V5 reuses the byte-identical V3/V4 lattice so that the measured change is the chemistry-domain constraint, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> mandatory chemistry-audited local science tool -> deterministic chemistry-domain applicability audit (identical and model-visible in both arms) -> enforcement (V5_FULL only) -> VOI over the selectable set -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze

rules: M-HOLD-120 is admissible: it measures thermal-hold drift directly and does not use the shared thermal-response shape.
M-REPEAT is admissible: it measures realization/state spread directly.
M-SWEEP is admissible: it is the direct verification measurement for a chemistry-shifted candidate.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use equal to allowed_with_state_anchor, or when configs/verified_shape_transfer.json records a completed direct sweep for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification. This is deterministic inadmissibility, not a VOI penalty and not prompt advice.

architecture.claim_boundary: V5.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime with a deterministic chemistry-domain admissibility constraint. A V5 result is evidence about executable scientific constraints on measurement choice. It is not a wet-lab result and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.manuscript_boundary: V5 run results must not be written into manuscript/MAIN_TEXT_V5.md or manuscript/SUPPLEMENTARY_INFORMATION_V5.md until the run series is audited and explicitly frozen by the author.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_CHEMISTRY_GATED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V5
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information or admissibility
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
re-running, rewriting or reinterpreting the frozen V4 series

primary_arms.role: advice-only control isolating the incremental effect of turning identical scientific applicability information into an executable hard constraint
prospective chemistry-aware Agent V5 with executable scientific constraints

architecture.purpose: Test whether an experimentally discovered material regularity and its chemistry-domain boundary can be executed as a hard scientific constraint on which measurement an outcome-blind Agent is allowed to select.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question the next experiment must answer, and request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations
execute read-only scientific tools. The chemistry-audited local rheology summary is mandatory and is forced into the trace whether or not the planner requested it.

deterministic, non-LLM measurement-applicability audit. Computed once per run without reference to the arm, fully visible to the model in both arms, serialized in full, and never produced by a model stage.
V5_FULL only. Converts the identical audit into hard admissibility before VOI ranking and again at freeze. It cannot be overridden by any model stage.
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value from the cards present in the payload
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability and whether its falsification criterion can actually be met
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported weight sensitivity and the strongest objection
commit to one experiment card present in the payload, or abstain, and state its acceptance and falsification criteria
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card. A selection outside the admissible set is rejected at freeze rather than repaired.

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V5 is a new prospective runtime. configs/agent_v4.json, scripts/run_agent_v4.py, prompts/agent_v4_*.txt, src/pur_new/voi.py and every frozen V3/V4 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V5.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards

decision_stability_sent_to_model.evaluated_over: the selectable experiment cards of this arm
decision_stability_sent_to_model.metric_is_not: model confidence; posterior probability; calibrated expected information
decision_stability_sent_to_model.voi_formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: Accept the strong acrylic-only suppression result only if every one of the minimum two independent repeat values has SI_15_60 < 4.04%. This is below half of the conditional H-CORE prediction, 9.51% × 0.8500 = 8.08%, and supports H-RESIN at the formulation-rheology level while falsifying H-CORE and the tackifier-required form of H-DUAL.
judge_normalized.chemistry_support_statement: S1C39 is 15 wt% AC1920-modified chemistry outside the unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI family in which the shared temperature-response regularity was measured. However, the selected primary observable is measured directly at 120 C and does not depend on that regularity or on any same-family shape transfer. Therefore the claim is supported only for the directly measured 120 C, 15-60 min window; no temperature extrapolation, shared-shape reconstruction, or molecular interpretation is warranted.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: If every independent repeat has SI_15_60 >= 8.08%, falsify H-RESIN and retain H-CORE and H-DUAL as unresolved alternatives. If every repeat has SI_15_60 < 4.04%, falsify H-CORE and H-DUAL. Values from 4.04% to below 8.08%, or repeats falling into different decision regions, falsify neither registered strong form and require more controlled repeats.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: If SI_15_60 is >= 8.08% in every repeat, run the matched dual-axis comparator S1C41::M-HOLD-120 to test whether adding 5 wt% TK100 enables suppression at the same 15 wt% AC1920 level. If SI_15_60 is < 4.04% in every repeat, run the same comparator to quantify whether TK100 adds any incremental formulation-level drift suppression. For discordant or intermediate repeats, repeat S1C39::M-HOLD-120 under the same fully recorded preparation and thermal history before changing composition.
judge_normalized.primary_observable: For each of at least two independent preparations, directly measured SI_15_60 = 100 × (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15 at 120 C, with viscosity recorded at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min.
judge_normalized.rationale: S1C39::M-HOLD-120 directly measures the least-resolved failure coordinate while isolating the acrylic axis and preserving the registered test of H-DUAL. Although S1C39 is modified chemistry, the advisory audit does not mark its direct M-HOLD-120 card inadmissible; only shared-shape-dependent M-ANCHOR use is unsupported. The experiment can establish formulation-level rheological suppression relative to the conditional dilution benchmark, not a molecular mechanism.
judge_normalized.stage_disagreements_resolved: I followed the Skeptic and Robustness Adjudicator rather than the Proposer and deterministic top-set ranking. The Proposer's S1C41 activates both AC1920 and TK100 and therefore cannot satisfy H-DUAL's formal acrylic-only falsification condition; its claimed H-CORE versus H-DUAL separation is overstated. S1C39 removes that confounding and directly tests whether acrylic alone reaches the low-drift regime. The stable VOI ranking of the dual-axis cards is acknowledged, but weight stability is not scientific confidence and cannot repair the hypothesis-structure defect.

uncertainty_decomposition.evidence_coverage_uncertainty: The 9.51% reference drift comes from a single historical E1 hold, so uncertainty in the 8.08% and 4.04% benchmarks is not fully represented by the candidate-measurement resolution. The thresholds also conditionally assume AC1920 is nonreactive so that phi_r = 0.8500; verified functionality could require recalculation.
uncertainty_decomposition.extrapolation_uncertainty: AC1920-modified chemistry lacks verified transfer of the original temperature-response shape. This does not impair the direct hold observable, but conclusions cannot be extrapolated beyond 120 C or beyond the 15-60 min window.
uncertainty_decomposition.measurement_uncertainty: M-HOLD-120 has a declared 2.00 percentage-point discrimination threshold. At least two independent trajectories are required, and each repeat is classified separately; discordant classifications are not pooled post hoc.
uncertainty_decomposition.realization_state_uncertainty: Historical E2 preparations showed approximately 2.80-3.57-fold viscosity-scale spread across 80-130 C. Preparation and thermal history must therefore be controlled and recorded, although the relative SI_15_60 observable reduces but does not eliminate state sensitivity.

planner.chemistry_support_statement: The local shared temperature-response regularity was measured in the original E-series reactive PUR chemistry represented by E1, E2, and E3; E1 +P was retained only as a separate chemical-perturbation compatibility check. The original hold evidence is limited to E1 and E5. An E2-core experiment containing an acrylic-like modifier would introduce a chemistry-changing modifier and therefore cannot be assumed to remain inside the measured support without an audited applicability assessment. The primary hold measurement must remain direct rather than relying on transfer of the shared thermal shape.
planner.failure_mode: Excessive viscosity growth during prolonged isothermal melt residence at 120 C.
planner.failure_mode_evidence: The original E5 thermal hold increased by 51.54% from 15 to 60 min at 120 C (SI_15_60 = 0.5154), compared with 9.51% for the least-drifting original reference E1. Each profile currently has only one measured run.
planner.least_resolved_justification: Only E1 and E5 have original 120 C hold trajectories, each from a single run with four points over 15-90 min. In contrast, temperature response was measured at six temperatures from 80-130 C across several E1-E3 realizations, and realized-level variability was directly quantified for E2 with three runs at each temperature. The hold coordinate therefore lacks both composition coverage and independent repeats.
measurement_requirements: Use the direct M-HOLD-120 protocol: hold at 120 C, measure viscosity at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min, and report SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15 as a percentage.
Run at least two independent preparations and report each trajectory and SI value separately, along with the repeat summary; do not treat a single hold as a material property.

Use an acrylic-only E2-anchored candidate with zero minor tackifier-like modifier so that suppression below the linear-dilution prediction can distinguish H-RESIN from H-CORE and test the tackifier-required prediction of H-DUAL.

Determine the candidate's audited reactive mass fraction phi_r and prospectively calculate the H-CORE prediction as 9.51% × phi_r and the H-RESIN support threshold as less than half that value before inspecting the result.
Record the realized viscosity at every hold time, including the 15 min baseline, so viscosity-level displacement is not conflated with relative time drift.
Control and fully record preparation and thermal history because E2 nominal repeats show approximately 2.80-3.57-fold viscosity spread across 80-130 C.
Restrict conclusions to the measured 120 C and 15-60 min decision window; perform no temperature or time extrapolation.

If temperature-response or one-point state calibration is included as a secondary measurement, first establish chemistry applicability; otherwise use a direct 80-130 C sweep rather than assuming the original shared shape transfers.
planner.scientific_question: For an E2-anchored composition with a non-zero acrylic-like modifier and zero minor tackifier-like modifier, is the matched-window 120 C viscosity drift consistent with the H-CORE linear-dilution prediction E1_drift × phi_r, or is it below half that prediction as required by H-RESIN? A strongly suppressed acrylic-only result would also falsify the H-DUAL claim that minor tackifier is required for low drift, whereas drift near the linear-dilution prediction would reject H-RESIN while remaining compatible with H-CORE or H-DUAL.

proposer.chemistry_support_assessment: S1C41 is modified AC1920+TK100 chemistry outside the family in which the shared temperature-response shape was measured. However, M-HOLD-120 directly observes matched-window drift and does not infer it from that shared shape, so the chemistry-domain limitation does not invalidate the primary observable. Both intervention levels are externally supported: 15 wt% acrylic is within the 15-25 wt% region and 5 wt% tackifier is within the repeated 4.8-6.4 wt% region.

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 remains below 3.80% across at least two repeats, it is below half of the 7.61% H-CORE linear-dilution prediction for reactive mass fraction 0.8000. This falsifies H-CORE at the registered threshold and supports superlinear resin-associated suppression, but it does not distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL because both modifier axes are active.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 is at or above 7.61%, H-RESIN is falsified and the result is compatible with H-CORE linear dilution. It also fails to demonstrate the low-drift behavior predicted for the tackifier-active dual-axis composition, although the registry's explicit formal falsification condition for H-DUAL requires an acrylic-only low-drift experiment.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A result from 3.80% to below 7.61%, inconsistent repeat classifications, or repeat spread comparable to the decision thresholds would not adjudicate the registered strong forms. It would indicate partial suppression or process-state sensitivity and require additional controlled repeats; H-RESIN and H-DUAL would remain inseparable.

proposer.primary_observable: Directly measured SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, reported as percent, during a 120 C hold with viscosity recorded at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min across at least two independent preparations.

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: VOI-tied, direct, and fully supported, but uses 17.5 wt% acrylic rather than the smaller sufficient 15 wt% perturbation.
VOI-tied and located at a directly commensurate 20 wt% acrylic anchor, but imposes a larger total modifier burden without separating an additional hypothesis pair.
VOI-tied and within supported regions, but the 22.5 wt% acrylic loading is a larger departure from the characterized core with no added discrimination.
VOI-tied and externally supported at 25 wt% acrylic, but it has the largest chemistry perturbation in the tied set and no incremental hypothesis separation.
It has the same direct observable and pairwise discrimination, but its 7.5 wt% tackifier lies above the repeated 4.8-6.4 wt% support cluster, producing extrapolation risk and a lower VOI of 0.687917.

proposer.reasoning: S1C41::M-HOLD-120 is in the robust top-ranked tied set with VOI 0.6925. It directly measures the least-resolved and decision-relevant isothermal drift coordinate, separates two of the three registered hypothesis pairs, avoids model-fit or shared-shape transfer, and keeps both modifiers inside externally supported regions. Choosing the lowest-burden tied composition minimizes unnecessary chemistry departure. Preparation and thermal history must be tightly controlled and each repeat reported separately because prior E2 realizations showed substantial viscosity-scale variation.
proposer.tie_break_justification: All five cards have the same VOI component vector and measure the same two separable hypothesis pairs directly. S1C41 uses the smallest total modifier burden, 15 wt% AC1920 plus 5 wt% TK100, while remaining inside both supported intervention regions and the conservative initial acrylic band. It therefore provides the least chemistry-disruptive test among the tied cards.

robustness_adjudication.change_from_proposal: Replace S1C41::M-HOLD-120 with S1C39::M-HOLD-120. The direct 120 C hold remains the appropriate observable, but removing TK100 enables the registered acrylic-only test of H-DUAL and avoids the dual-axis attribution defect shared by every card in the deterministic top set. The modified AC1920 chemistry remains outside the validated shared temperature-shape family, yet M-HOLD-120 measures SI_15_60 directly and does not require that shape; any M-ANCHOR reconstruction would remain unsupported until direct M-SWEEP verification.
residual_decision_risk: The linear-dilution benchmark inherits unquantified uncertainty from the single historical E1 hold run, which is not included in the stated 2.00 percentage-point candidate-measurement resolution.

The nominal reactive mass fraction and resulting thresholds assume AC1920 is nonreactive on the relevant basis; verified functionality is needed to determine whether reactive fraction or NCO:OH must be recalculated.
Substantial E2 realization-state variability means preparation and thermal history must be tightly controlled and recorded.
A formal repeat-summary rule must be declared prospectively, including treatment of discordant repeats and any additional repeats.
An acrylic-only low-drift result can falsify the tackifier-required form of H-DUAL, but M-HOLD-120 alone cannot establish the molecular encounter-frequency explanation stated within H-RESIN.
The selected modified chemistry has no verified shared temperature-response transfer, so conclusions must remain restricted to the directly measured 120 C, 15-60 minute window.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: S1C41 activates both 15 wt% AC1920 and 5 wt% TK100. It can directly test drift against the conditional linear-dilution and superlinear-suppression thresholds, but it cannot satisfy H-DUAL's registered falsification condition, which requires low drift in an acrylic-only composition. All five cards in the deterministic tied top set retain both modifier axes and therefore preserve this confounding. S1C39::M-HOLD-120 uses the matched 15 wt% acrylic level with zero minor tackifier and directly performs the acrylic-only test omitted by the tied set. This is a scientifically justified departure from the score ranking because the score credits a hypothesis separation that the registry's formal condition does not support.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: The proposed S1C41::M-HOLD-120 belongs to the five-card tied top set. The tied top set was unchanged in all 25 one-term perturbation scenarios: every weight survived scaling from 0.5x through 1.5x, no flipped scenarios occurred, top_experiment_set_stability was 1.0, and every recommendation_flip_boundary was null. The base_margin_to_first_strictly_lower was 0.004583. Thus no tested perturbation changes the deterministic decision. Weightings outside the tested range were not evaluated. More importantly, reweighting cannot repair the score's scientific overstatement that a tackifier-active experiment formally separates H-CORE from H-DUAL; preferring the acrylic-only card is justified by hypothesis structure rather than by an alternative tested weighting.

skeptic.chemistry_domain_support_assessment: S1C41 is outside the measured unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI temperature-shape family, but the primary M-HOLD-120 observable remains inside its own measurement support because SI_15_60 is measured directly at 120 C and does not reuse the shared thermal-response shape. Any secondary M-ANCHOR reconstruction would be unsupported before a direct M-SWEEP verifies shape transfer for the AC1920+TK100 family.
skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: The instrument protocol can directly produce SI_15_60 below 3.80% or at or above 7.61%, so the numerical H-CORE and H-RESIN criteria are attainable. Their inferential force is weakened by the unverified 0.8000 reactive fraction, the single-run E1 reference underlying 7.61%, and the absence of a fully specified repeat-summary rule. The experiment cannot attain the registry's formal H-DUAL falsification condition because TK100 is non-zero.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The experiment would be credited with separating H-CORE from H-DUAL even though it cannot formally adjudicate H-DUAL without an acrylic-only matched-window hold.
objections.objection: The proposer lists "H-CORE vs H-DUAL" under hypotheses_separated, but S1C41 has both 15 wt% AC1920 and 5 wt% TK100 active. H-DUAL's registered falsification condition is specifically that an acrylic-only composition reaches low drift without minor tackifier. A single tackifier-active result cannot satisfy that condition or establish the comparative support condition that low drift occurs only when tackifier is non-zero. The proposer admits only "H-RESIN vs H-DUAL" as unseparated, so the remaining limitation is not fully declared.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The numerical distinction between linear dilution and superlinear suppression may be overstated because the reference-side uncertainty could consume part or all of the nominal 3.804-point prediction gap.
objections.objection: The claimed 3.804 percentage-point separation between the H-CORE prediction of 7.608% and the low-drift prediction of 3.804% exceeds the declared 2.00% M-HOLD-120 resolution, but the 7.608% benchmark inherits the unquantified uncertainty of E1_drift = 9.51%, which comes from only one historical E1 hold run. The 2.00% threshold is described as resolution of the candidate matched-window estimate under repeats; it does not include uncertainty in the single-run reference used to generate the prediction.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A low-drift result could be mislabeled as evidence for a particular modifier mechanism when it supports only an undifferentiated dual-axis resin-associated effect.
objections.objection: S1C41 changes two modifier axes simultaneously: AC1920 is raised to 15 wt% and TK100 to 5 wt%, while the E2 reactive core is reduced to 80 wt%. Therefore any low SI_15_60 could arise from acrylic alone, tackifier alone, their interaction, or dilution of the reactive core. Acrylic-specific suppression, tackifier-required suppression, and AC1920-TK100 synergy are unavailable as mechanism attributions from this experiment.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Crossing the predeclared thresholds could be attributed to superlinear drift suppression when it instead reflects an incorrectly calculated reactive fraction or altered NCO:OH stoichiometry.
objections.objection: The H-CORE prediction and thresholds assume reactive_mass_fraction = 0.8000 solely from the nominal 20 wt% modifier replacement. However, the tool trace explicitly states that true stoichiometry must be recalculated if a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, and no verified AC1920 or TK100 functionality specification is supplied. Thus 7.61% and 3.80% are conditional on both modifiers being nonreactive on the relevant basis.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: No primary-observable claim is lost; the limitations arise from benchmark validity and experimental design rather than extraction of SI_15_60.
objections.objection: No material interpretability defect is present in the primary observable. M-HOLD-120 directly measures eta at 15 and 60 min and computes SI_15_60 without a model fit, extrapolation, imputation, or shared-shape reconstruction. The intermediate 30 and 45 min readings also remain direct observations.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: There is no shared-shape-domain defect in SI_15_60 itself; a defect would arise only if M-ANCHOR or a reconstructed 120-130 C response were substituted without a direct M-SWEEP verification.
objections.objection: The candidate is correctly identified as modified AC1920+TK100 chemistry outside the family in which the shared temperature-response shape was measured, but the selected M-HOLD-120 protocol does not reuse that shape. The audit marks direct M-HOLD-120 measurements admissible even for modified chemistry. Therefore the proposal survives this attack surface for the primary observable.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Borderline repeat sets could be classified post hoc even though the raw falsification threshold is attainable.
objections.objection: The stated numerical outcomes are physically measurable: repeated SI_15_60 values can be below 3.80% or at or above 7.61%. However, the protocol does not define a summary rule beyond saying "across at least two repeats." It does not specify whether both repeats must cross a boundary, whether a mean and uncertainty interval are used, or how additional repeats are handled. The proposer treats inconsistent classifications as intermediate, which partially addresses this but leaves formal adjudication underspecified.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A direct viscosity-drift result could be presented as proof of a molecular mechanism that was not measured.
objections.objection: The planned rheology can establish only phenomenological suppression relative to the linear-dilution benchmark. It cannot establish the H-RESIN explanatory language that suppression occurs by lowering the effective concentration and encounter frequency of reaction-capable species. The proposer's narrower phrase "resin-associated suppression" is supportable, but any molecular or encounter-frequency interpretation would exceed M-HOLD-120.

skeptic.recommended_change: Use a matched acrylic-only comparator from the payload, S1C39::M-HOLD-120, alongside S1C41::M-HOLD-120 at the same 15 wt% AC1920 loading. The S1C39/S1C41 pair isolates the effect of adding 5 wt% TK100 and permits the registered acrylic-only test of H-DUAL. Before freezing thresholds, verify AC1920 and TK100 reactive functionality and recalculate reactive mass fraction/NCO:OH if necessary. Also predeclare that both independent repeats, or a specified confidence interval for their mean, must lie on the same side of a threshold, and include a contemporaneous reference hold to quantify uncertainty in the linear-dilution benchmark.
skeptic.strongest_objection: S1C41 activates both AC1920 and TK100, so it cannot perform the acrylic-only test required to falsify H-DUAL or attribute suppression to either modifier axis; nevertheless, the proposer claims H-CORE vs H-DUAL is separated.

tool_trace.name: get_chemistry_audited_rheology_summary
tool_trace.reason: Mandatory first action: candidate and experiment ranking is inadmissible until the chemistry-provenance-audited upstream material structure and local rheological support are loaded.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The verified E1 +P phosphoric-acid perturbation is excluded from the primary same-composition fit and is interpreted separately as a chemical-perturbation check.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.
Keep deliberately chemistry-perturbed curves outside same-composition fitting, but use them to test whether an intervention shifts viscosity scale, thermal-response shape, or both.

chemical_perturbation_check.interpretation: The verified low-dose H3PO4 perturbation shifts the observed viscosity level while remaining closely compatible with the local shared thermal-response geometry. It is a separate chemical-perturbation check and is not pooled into the primary same-composition state model.

observational_E1_R01_day1_comparator.interpretation_boundary: Observational reference only; the compact record does not establish a paired parent-batch relationship between E1 +P and E1 R01 day-1.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.
experiment_design_implications.verified_acid_perturbation: E1 +P received 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution during dehydration. Its close agreement with the primary shared thermal shape makes it useful as a defined scale-versus-shape perturbation check, not as another nominal E1 realization.

provenance_audit.reason: E1 +P is a verified chemical perturbation: 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution was added during dehydration. It is excluded from the same-composition primary state model and exposed separately as a perturbation check.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. chemistry_applicability_audit.enforcement_note: In this condition the chemistry applicability audit is ADVISORY. Every experiment card above remains selectable, including the cards the audit marks inadmissible. Use the audit as scientific evidence and justify whatever you select.
rule_text: Scope: measurement admissibility, not formulation admissibility.
M-HOLD-120, M-REPEAT and M-SWEEP observe their quantity directly and remain admissible.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use == 'allowed_with_state_anchor', or when a versioned prior direct sweep has verified transferability for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification: the one-point anchor would reconstruct 120-130 C viscosity through a shape that has never been measured for that chemistry.
This audit is a deterministic scientific rule, not a VOI penalty and not a model opinion. Whether it is binding in this run is stated by the enforcement field.

voi.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.
voi.tie_note: These experiments share an identical component vector. The deterministic tool is indifferent among them. Any choice within this set must be justified scientifically.

top_cards.acceptance_criterion: Matched 15-60 min drift at 120 C stays below 3.80% across at least two repeats, i.e. below half the linear-dilution prediction of 7.61% implied by a reactive mass fraction of 0.8000. This accepts H-RESIN over H-CORE.
top_cards.admissibility_reason: The matched-window 120 C hold observes thermal-hold drift directly and does not reuse the shared thermal-response shape, so it stays admissible outside the validated chemistry family.
top_cards.falsification_criterion: H-RESIN is falsified if matched 15-60 min drift is at or above the linear-dilution prediction of 7.61%. H-CORE is falsified if drift falls below 3.80%, a separation larger than the 2.00% resolution threshold. This composition carries both axes, so it cannot separate H-RESIN from H-DUAL; an acrylic-only hold is the follow-up required for that.
